Market astrology calendar, 24 Nov – 31 Dec 2026

S&P 500, BSE Sensex, gold and silver. Dates and times US Eastern (IST also shown for changes). Sidereal Lahiri, mean node, whole-sign drishti; Solar return uses tropical signs, as its method does. Built 27 Nov 2026 17:02 ET from prices to the 23 Nov 2026 close. Market prices and astrology only.

Read this first

  • What each market line shows: our signal-table label (Bullish / Bearish with High, Moderate or Low strength), and the combined model's chance of a rise over the next 5 sessions. Green and red mean at least 2 points above or below that market's normal rate.
  • How much to trust it: over 2013–2026 the combined model's calls were right 55% (S&P), 54% (Sensex), 54% (gold) and 51% (silver) of the time over 5 sessions: a small edge at best. Every probability in this calendar stays within a few points of normal. Treat them as leanings.
  • Solar return is the NYSE monthly solar-return method you shared. Its daily calls here are generated by us the Solar return way; they reproduce 8 of the 9 days Solar return called, but over 1928–2026 the same rule was at chance.
  • What has shown some edge: Jupiter sextile Venus (bullish over 5 sessions), the bearish calendar fortnight rule “Three Saturdays in Shukla Paksha”, robust volatility factors (more big days, no direction) and the Mars–Jupiter–node lead (a lead, not proven).
  • Paap Kartari: Jupiter is hemmed by Ketu and Mars (2026 document B117) from 16 Nov to 31 Jan 2027, and Mercury enters Paap Kartari (B116) on 1 Jan 2027. Their 2000–2026 records are in each day's notes, and January is checked market by market in the January 2027 section: Mercury's version held up as bearish on the Sensex only; Jupiter's showed more big days, not significant. Shubh Kartari is in none of our sources; tested anyway, it did not work and is not used.
  • Not used: dashas (tested, no edge; parked at your request), news and fundamentals.

Gold: Jupiter's afflictions in past crashes (your note)

The note: in the gold crashes of 1974, 1980, 2008, 2011, 2020, 2022 and 2026 Jupiter was in trine / mutual aspect / conjunction with Saturn, or with a node or Pluto, or hemmed by malefics, and under the Vedha of malefics. Reading: the positions are mostly right, with sidereal corrections: at the Jan 1980 peak Saturn was in Virgo (it returned to Leo with Jupiter and Rahu from about March 1980); at the Aug 2011 peak Saturn was in Virgo (Libra only from 15 Nov 2011); at the Jan 2026 peak Jupiter was retrograde in Gemini (in Cancer, trine Saturn, from June 2026). Malefic Vedha on Jupiter occurred at some point in every fall, but the fast Sun and Mars make that true in most stretches. Taken together, “Jupiter afflicted” holds in 69% of all months, so it cannot single out crashes; the Jupiter–Saturn trine was present at 3 of 8 crash peaks against 16% of months, a lead from a small sample.
When the current one ends: Jupiter with Ketu in Leo ends on 5 Dec 2026 (Ketu enters Cancer). The pattern returns when Jupiter goes back into Cancer: Jupiter with Ketu 2026-11-25 – 2026-12-05; 2027-01-25 – 2027-06-25; Jupiter–Saturn trine 2027-01-25 – 2027-06-02; 2027-06-26 – 2027-10-19; malefic Vedha on Jupiter 2026-12-06 – 2027-04-09; 2027-06-26 – 2027-11-03; 2027-12-24 – 2027-12-31; all together 2027-01-25 – 2027-04-09; 2027-06-26 – 2027-10-19; 2027-12-24 – 2027-12-31.
Bottom and recovery watch (gold_turns_ET.html): at gold's 24 bottoms since 1972, a Jupiter direct station within ±30 days (33% vs 15% of weeks) and Jupiter–Saturn within 10° of trine / opposition / conjunction (42% vs 20%) were the most common features; a Saturn direct station within ±30 days was next (29% vs 16%). For the current fall that points to two watch windows: 11 Nov 2026 – 10 Jan 2027 (Saturn stations direct 11 Dec at Pisces 13.7°) and 14 Mar – 13 May 2027 (Jupiter stations direct 13 Apr at Cancer 22.75°, with Ketu within 0.5°, Mars nearby and Saturn trine within 1.4°). The Jupiter–Saturn trine was equally common at peaks, and about 40 features were tested, so these are watch periods, not timing rules.

Every computable rule from the three books added on 27 Nov 2026 was backtested: 113 results in new_sources_test_ET.html and 84 in new_sources_leftover_ET.html, using the §6 method with Benjamini–Hochberg correction. None holds, so none of them feeds the signals or the probabilities. They are shown here and in each day as information, each with its test result.

Worth knowing:
  • Brihat Samhita 42.6 with its eclipse condition: 2026 qualifies (lunar eclipse of 28 Aug, Sun in sidereal Leo), so the stated sell window is 16 Dec 2026 – 14 Jan 2027. But eclipse years did worse than other years: gold rose by mid-December in 6 of 14 eclipse years, against 22 of 39 other years.
  • Lord of the year 2026–27 (Chaitra new moon 2026-03-19): Mercury by US time, Jupiter by Indian time; both are 'good' lords. Watch list only: on the S&P 1929–2026, years with good lords were up 76% vs 64% (p 0.047), but it weakens to p 0.10 with the Indian weekday.
  • NYSE annual chart (2026-05-21 10:40 ET): the Tajika ruler of the year is Moon (triplicity lord), strength 12.44 of 20, in house 1; the muntha is in house 7. By the text that means a good year with the muntha in a weak house, but both rules test at chance.
  • Eclipse rules (eclipse in Libra or Sagittarius; eclipse in the lunar month Chaitra, 'dealers in gold suffer'): nominal p < 0.05 on gold and silver only, from 9–20 cases. No such eclipse falls before 2028, so there is nothing to watch in this calendar.

Every sky event of the week backtested. 59 event classes (exact aspects, sign and nakshatra entries, tithi, yoga, Bhadra, the last quarter) were each scored on every occurrence since 2000 on the S&P 500, Sensex, gold and silver: 460 tests. 0 pass the Benjamini–Hochberg correction, and 3 have a nominal p < 0.05. Reading: the astronomy is right except Venus–Mercury, which form no aspect in 30 Nov – 5 Dec (24–28° apart). Since 1928 the Full Moon near Uranus came with twice the usual number of sharp reversals (14 vs 6.5, p 0.007), but all of the excess is in 1977–2026 (none in 1928–1976) and big days were normal: a lead, not a rule. Sun opposite Uranus and Mars square Uranus showed no reliable effect. In the last 250 sessions a short window had a big day or a sharp reversal about 15% of the time, so “volatility” calls in the current market are often right by default.

Why the Sensex scored higher than the S&P

  • Same labels for both indices. The market table only uses rules that held on both indices, so its label was identical for the S&P and the Sensex on 16 of 16 weekdays in 1–23 Nov and 40 of 40 labelled days in the last 60 days.
  • The markets went opposite ways. Over the 60 days the S&P fell 6.1% while the Sensex rose 10.2%. In 1–23 Nov the Sensex rose on 12 of 15 days, the S&P on 6 of 16.
  • The labels leaned bullish (mostly Bullish in November). A bullish label is right in a rising market and wrong in a falling one, so the same call scored high on the Sensex and low on the S&P. A rule that said “up” every day would have scored the same.
  • Over the long run the S&P is no worse: 2013–2026 walk-forward, 5 sessions: S&P 55%, Sensex 54%.
  • No timing advantage: each day's Sensex session (09:15–15:30 IST) ends before the New York day starts; labels come from astrology only, so there is no look-ahead.
  • Conclusion: the higher Sensex score reflects which way each market moved, not better astrology for India.

What did not work and is not used

  • Dashas at every level and as classical combinations (0 of 132 tests held): parked.
  • Solar return monthly chart indications (1,186 months: no edge); its daily rules apart from Jupiter sextile Venus: at chance.
  • Most catalogue rules on market direction: at chance after multiple-testing correction (see the tables' “supported” filter).
